newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Equitable aims for top five spot by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Equitable aims for top five spot by 2000.

text.p: Equitable Banking Corp said on Thursday it is aiming to join the elite "Magic 5" ranks of the country's biggest banks by the year 2000.

Currently the ninth largest bank, Equitable Bank is expanding its reach by intensifying its consumer loan business as well as venturing into investment and trust banking, president Wilfrido Vergara told reporters during the public listing of its shares.
"We seek to fortify our middle-income market ... We will (also) go heavily into consumer banking, and even to the upscale market," Vergara said.
"There's always the Magic 5 that they talk about. We would like to think that we will be in the top five within this decade," he said.
The industry is led by Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co Inc, Bank of the Philippine Islands, Philippine Commercial International Bank, Far East Bank and Trust Co Inc and the Philippine National Bank.
Equitable is projecting its net income to breach the 2.0 billion peso mark this year as against 1.046 billion pesos posted last year.
In the first quarter alone, the bank's net income reached about 315 million pesos, 25 percent higher than what was registered in the same period last year.
"We see ourselves performing at a pace that is faster than the sector where we're in," he said.
The bank is one of the few banks that cater to the affluent Chinese-Filipino community.
He said that while other banks seek for cheaper sources of funds to stay competitive, especially with the entry of foreign banks, Equitable would have enough funds to meet the growing demand.
"Our build-up in the capital is timely since we now have access to funds that we can redeploy and build leverage on at an opportune time," Vergara said.

The bank generated 7.0 billion pesos from offering 62,172,820 of its shares to the public. It also sold warrants, which have 23.24 million underlying shares. The warrants can be exercised within 12 months from listing.

Equitable debuted strongly amid a declining stock market. It closed at 117 pesos on high turnover from its offering price of 113.30 pesos. It hit a high of 121 in early trade after opening at 118 pesos. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
